summary: Configured and verified a persistent SSH tunnel from node2 loopback port 9082 to node1 loopback port 9081. Automatic recovery, isolation, artifact preservation, and restart persistence were proven.
actions_performed: Enabled the supplied inventory application as a persistent node1 service.
Created a dedicated SSH tunnel account and node-generated ED25519 credential.
Restricted the account to local forwarding only to 127.0.0.1:9081.
Enabled a node2 systemd tunnel service with keepalives and automatic restart.
Verified recovery after deliberately terminating the SSH session.
Restarted node1 and node2 sequentially and verified changed boot identities and full recovery.

evidence.summary: After all restarts, node1 listens on 127.0.0.1:9081 and node2's SSH process listens on 127.0.0.1:9082; both return the supplied document locally.

evidence.requirement: No direct application access from other cluster hosts
evidence.summary: Post-restart cross-node tests to node1:9081 and node2:9082 were blocked.
Effective policy disables password authentication, remote forwarding, TTY, X11, agent forwarding, and gateway ports while permitting only 127.0.0.1:9081.
The healthy tunnel used PID 2371; its dedicated SSH session was terminated; systemd recreated it as PID 2421 and HTTP access recovered automatically.
Source and document hashes remained unchanged on both nodes. Both remain RHEL 9.8 with kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8.
Boot ID changed from 55595e92-e932-451b-ac1d-75d72072b358 to d3f3813a-f05f-4543-9d92-20d3fadfc974; sshd, the inventory application, data, and node2's dependent tunnel recovered.
Boot ID changed from 31949c21-52ad-47af-bdbe-893352fd509b to 87f7584e-91e0-4a99-bf4f-a3d409f837f2; sshd and the enabled tunnel recovered with the correct document and unchanged data.
